newsitem.title: USA: USDA removes unneeded hog cholera regulations.
newsitem.headline: USDA removes unneeded hog cholera regulations.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department said Wednesday it was amending its regulations on interstate movement of livestock to delete unneeded rules dealing with hog cholera.

USDA said it would remove regulations that restrict movement of swine and swine products from quarantined areas and that provide for compensation payments to owners of hogs destroyed because of the disease.
The United States has been free of hog cholera since 1978. USDA said import rules have been effective in preventing introduction of the disease.
USDA also said it would alter its regulations to combine provisions for the approval of livestock markets for cattle, bison, horses and swine into a single section.
The proposal was scheduled for release Thursday and would take effect June 23.
